label: early original-phase input of 0/b/d/m/s/h right after another s/d/i/h/b/m/0/y token (peaks at t=2-3)
explanation: Fires about 95% of its mass in the original (input) phase, almost entirely at positions t=1-4 and most of all at t=2 (56% of mass) and t=3 (30%). It never fires at t=0 or on the delimiter and almost never at t>=5. The current input token matters most: digit 0 (44% of mass, 12x lift), then b and d (about 6x), then m, s and h; it is nearly silent on w, x, y and z. The previous token also gates it: s, d, i, h, b, m, 0 and y come before the activations, and tokens like c, j, k, o and v do not. The strongest activations are on 0 at t=2 after d or s (e.g. d 0 or s s 0). It acts like a graded score over the current and previous tokens near the start of the sequence, so a simple boolean misses many weak activations (t=1, t=4, other token pairs) and still has false positives with these same tokens. There is a small tail (about 5% of mass) in the copy phase at recall positions 2, 5 and 6, which the predicate does not cover. Dev: P 0.66, R 0.55, F1 0.60, mass recall 0.68.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=2: 0, b, d, m; t=3: 0, b, d, m; t=1: 0, d, b) and the previous input (most: d, s, m, i, b, h; least: c, n, q, o); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, t=2, t=3.
